title: Chandra Unmasks a Supernova Impostor Star (Nov. 9, 2026)
description:
A star about 30 million light-years away, AT 2016blu in the galaxy NGC 4559, has erupted at least 27 times between 2012 and 2026, with outbursts that resemble supernova explosions, yet it survives each one. NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory caught it in outburst in March 2026, at least 100 times brighter in X-rays than in 2001 to 2002, before the outbursts began. The best explanation, from a study published Nov. 9, 2026 in The Astrophysical Journal: a previously hidden black hole or neutron star pulls material off the star every 113 days as they orbit. Next: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on Wednesday, Nov. 18.
